## MF-1 — The shadow guard skips the exact motivating incident (VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY)

Raised by: Codex alternatives (FATAL). Corroborated from a different angle by Claude
alternatives (concern 1). **Orchestrator verified the factual chain directly.**

Plan §4.4's shadow guard permits resolution of a mapped local name only if its import alias
is that name's SOLE module-wide binding, counting `ast.alias` bindings "exactly as
`_exclusive_use_sole_binding` does".

The pre-fix #2223 driver imports `hub` at THREE separate places, all the same target.
Verified at AST level against `git show 1b9ae765b6~1:scripts/issue2223_drift.py`:

```
total module-wide bindings of 'hub': 3
  alias  line 715   module=explore_persona_space.orchestrate
  alias  line 740   module=explore_persona_space.orchestrate
  alias  line 2497  module=explore_persona_space.orchestrate
SOLE-BINDING RULE (plan 4.4 as written) => ABSTAIN (skip)
```

The incident call sits at line 2509:
`url = hub._upload(at, f"{HF_EXPERIMENT}/analysis_tensors", repo_type="dataset")`

**Consequence.** Under §4.4 exactly as written, `hub` fails the shadow guard before S1 is
attempted, so the motivating call becomes a NOTED SKIP rather than a bind failure. The plan
cannot deliver its central claimed protection as drafted.

**Second consequence — an internal contradiction, confirmed LIVE inside the census itself.**
The binding reconciler verified something stronger than the historical-blob argument: the
CURRENT `scripts/issue2223_drift.py` — one of the 88 adopters in the §5 census — STILL imports
`hub` at three places (lines 716, 741, 3304). So §5's claimed row "Registered names with
non-import bindings (shadow-guard abstains): **0** across all 88" (plan line 209) is not merely
unverified, it is IMPOSSIBLE under §4.4 as written. That row is only satisfiable under a LOOSER
rule (non-import bindings disqualify; repeated same-target imports tolerated) — its own phrasing
betrays that the prototype measured the looser rule, not §4.4's sole-binding rule. The plan
cannot simultaneously implement §4.4 as written and reproduce its 193/193-bound / 0-skip
licensing baseline.

**The cited collector confirms the semantics.** `argcheck.py:151` `_exclusive_use_sole_binding`
returns `None` whenever `len(bindings) != 1`, appending each `ast.alias` as a separate binding
with NO same-target deduplication. Three same-target imports ⇒ 3 bindings ⇒ `None`. So §4.4's
"collected exactly as `_exclusive_use_sole_binding` does" is not loose drafting — the referenced
implementation really does behave this way.

**The planned test cannot catch this.** The §6 incident fixture (plan line 219) contains a
SINGLE `from explore_persona_space.orchestrate import hub`, so it passes under EITHER semantics
and would not surface the defect at implementation time. This is why the fixture requirement
below is not optional.

Claude alternatives measured the scale: **54 of 88 adopters import `hub` function-locally, only
7 at module level** — so a literal implementation would abstain on most of the fleet, and the
check would be near-vacuous while the plan claims full coverage.

**Required fix.** Treat repeated imports of the SAME registered target as COMPATIBLE bindings
(not conflicting) — the guard must discriminate a genuine shadow (a local `def`, a parameter, an
assignment rebinding the name to something else) from benign re-import of the same module. State
`_bind_import_map`'s position semantics explicitly: module-level, function-local, and repeated
imports of the same target all resolve. Then RE-RUN the census under the shipped resolver and
report the realized numbers. Add a regression fixture reproducing the historical
repeated-import layout (same name imported at ≥2 sites, one of them function-local) and assert
the incident-shaped call FAILS rather than skips.
